result.changelog: Fixed the 'error' items. The final battle now follows English Wikipedia: the Marines were sucked into space before the fleet destroyed the Doomseye, and Samus then recovered them. Added the Master Brain as the entity controlling the Doomseye (Nintendo Life recap; a WebSearch snippet of Wikitroid agrees). Samus is buried under debris after her defeat and returns to help against the Master Brain. The incident, Doomseye and Miles entries no longer say the Marines alone won the decisive fight. Unverified items: removed 'Project Golem' from content and keys; 'sensor bombs' became 'decoys and mines'; 'Samus never piloted a Mech' narrowed to the Bermuda campaign. 'Ice Titans captured for study' kept, confirmed by JP Wikipedia (ecological research). Nits and missing items: 27.2 km/h; official role names (attackers/assisters/healers/all-rounders); Shock Shot; freeze effect; Lone Wolf MOD barred from squads; AI Combat Drones; Hopper Nest forced the Federation out of Excelcion; Colossan/Shiranon descriptions corrected; 'toxic' and 'layered' dropped; 'all but one' missile base; Infestation operation and egg stolen from the Pirates; Miles's uniform has the same design as Adam Malkovich's, with a commander-only helmet. Removed unsupported color: 'armored' creature, 'rookie/newly graduated', 'recruits train in Blast Ball', Samus's reporting line, and the Bion civilization's survival motive. Keys: dropped bare 'Bermuda', 'Mech', 'Mechs', 'Pirate warship', 'Pirate battleship', 'Doom Eye' and the meta keys (post-credits, secret ending, epilogue). No primary keys overlap across entries any more. The egg entry was retitled 'The Metroid egg and Sylux's break-in'. Its link to Prime 4 is now a plain sequence of events (the Tanamaar attack, then Viewros), with no claim that those Metroids came from this egg. Fixed provenance and meta wording. All entries are 229-422 words; the incident entry is the domain's biggest subject.
result.unresolved: The Master Brain is attested only by Nintendo Life's recap and a Wikitroid search snippet; Metroid Wiki has no page for it. Its nature is unclear: a Mother Brain-like organism (Wikitroid snippet) or an AI supercomputer (villains wiki). Content calls it 'the entity controlling the ship'. Sources disagree on what dropped the Doomseye's shield (Wikipedia: Samus's defeat; Wikitroid snippet: the Master Brain powers it), so no cause is given. Nintendo Life calls Samus 'pivotal' in the Master Brain's defeat; content softens this to 'returned to assist'. English names are unverified for Goliath, Sokeen, Colossan, Shiranon, Hopper Nest, Mainframe and the Hugenate Beam, so content leaves them unnamed. The egg scene is a conditional ending in the source; content presents it as having happened. Metroid Wiki places the game between Metroid II and Super Metroid; the entries follow Wikipedia and Nintendo Life and place it after Corruption.
